x-axis is horizontal, points RIGHT (+x).
y-axis is vertical, points UP (+y).

In Ex 2: last col (RIGHT)

If the green line is vertical, it is ALWAYS the last column (RIGHT)!

Horizontal -> Top (row 0)
Vertical -> Right (last col)?
Wait, why not bottom or left?
Is there ANY training example with bottom or left? NO!
All horizontal ones (Ex 1, Ex 3) are row 0!
All vertical ones (Ex 2, Ex 4) are the rightmost column!

- If the two parallel lines are VERTICAL, the output line is VERTICAL!

For horizontal line: ALWAYS row 0?

If you take a vector:
(x, y) where x is horizontal (col), y is vertical (row).
Wait! In math, the positive x-axis points RIGHT.
The positive y-axis points UP.
In a matrix/grid:
UP is row 0 (decreasing row index)!
RIGHT is last col (increasing col index)!
Both UP and RIGHT are the POSITIVE directions of the Cartesian coordinate system: +Y is UP, +X is RIGHT!
Could that be it?!
